q: The works of the Kalidasa include:
options: He wrote the Abhijnanasakuntalam and the Malavikagnimitram and the Raghuvamsha
explanation: The Kalidasa wrote the Abhijnanasakuntalam, the Malavikagnimitram and the Vikramorvashiyam of the plays and the Raghuvamsha and the Kumarasambhava of the poems.

q: The Raghuvamsha of the Kalidasa is:
options: Is a drama of the Bhasa
Is the epic poem of the Kalidasa about the dynasty of the Ramas
explanation: The Raghuvamsha is the epic poem of the Kalidasa narrating the story of the Rama dynasty and it is one of the five great epics of the Sanskrit literature.

q: The 'Mṛchchhakatika' was written by:
explanation: The Mṛchchhakatika, the 'The Little Clay Cart', is the famous play of the Vishakhadatta, probably of the last century BCE, and it is a satire on the decadent society.

q: The thirteen plays of the Bhasa were:
options: rediscovered in 1912 and staged in 1955 by the K. Balachander
of the Sanskrit of the Chola period
explanation: The thirteen plays of the Bhasa were rediscovered in 1912 and they were staged in 1955 by the K. Balachander with the music of the M.S. Subbulakshmi.

q: The Sanskrit plays of the Harsha are:
options: The Harsha was a Buddhist monk
The Harsha wrote the Nagananda and the Ratnavali and the Priyadarshika
The Harsha wrote only the dramas
The Harsha wrote the epic poems
explanation: The Harsha, the last great emperor, wrote the three Sanskrit dramas of the Nagananda, the Ratnavali and the Priyadarshika, and he was a patron of the learning.

q: The Bhavabhuti wrote the:
options: He was the author of the Natyasastra
The Bhavabhuti wrote the Malatimadhava and the Uttararamacharita and the Mahaviracharita
explanation: The Bhavabhuti of the ninth century wrote the Malatimadhava, the Uttararamacharita and the Mahaviracharita, and he is considered the greatest of the Sanskrit dramatists after the Kalidasa.

q: The author of the Ashtadhyayi is:
options: The Panini wrote the Ashtadhyayi, the first grammar of the Sanskrit
explanation: The Panini wrote the Ashtadhyayi, the first systematic grammar of the Sanskrit, and the Patanjali wrote the Mahabhashya as a commentary on it.

q: The Kautilya and the Chanakya wrote the:
options: The Kautilya and the Chanakya wrote the Arthashastra and the Chanakya was the adviser of the Chandragupta
explanation: The Kautilya, the author of the Arthashastra, is also identified with the Chanakya, the adviser and the prime minister of the Chandragupta Maurya.

q: The 'Harshacharita' was written by:
explanation: The Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita, the biography of the Harsha, and the Kadamba is the Dandin who wrote the Dasakumaracharita.

q: The Dandin wrote the:
options: The Dandin wrote the Dasakumaracharita in the sixth century
The Dandin was of the Gupta period
He was of the Mughal period
explanation: The Dandin, a court poet of the Harsha's time, wrote the Dasakumaracharita, a prose romance in the six chapters, in the sixth century.

q: The Naisadha is the:
options: It is a drama of the Kalidasa
The Naiṣadha is the first great Sanskrit romance by the Vatsa
explanation: The Naiṣadha, by the Vatsa, is the first great Sanskrit romance and the Bhattikavya of the Dandin and the Vasavadatta of the Subandhu are the other early romances.

q: The Sangam literature of the early centuries CE is:
options: a Sangam era collection of the temple songs
the Buddhist literature of the Tamil
the corpus of the ancient Tamil poetry
explanation: The Sangam literature, the corpus of the ancient Tamil poetry in the early centuries CE, consists of the eight anthologies and the ten idylls and it is the earliest of the Tamil literature.

q: Which of the following statements regarding the The Tiruvalluvar is correct?
explanation: The Tirukkural, the classic of the Tamil literature, is a work of the Tiruvalluvar, who is also the author of the Tiruppavai and the Tiruvempavai.

q: The 'Silappatikaram' was written by:
explanation: The Silappatikaram, one of the five great epics of the Tamil literature, was written by the Ilango Adigal, a Chera prince and a Jain monk.

q: The Subramaniyan of the Subramania Bharati is:
options: an epic of the Tamil literature
explanation: The Subramaniyan, the unfinished epic of the Subramania Bharati, is one of the landmarks of the modern Tamil literature and he also wrote the Kuyil and the Mahakavi.

q: The Bharathi of the Tamil is:
options: The Bharathi was the Mahakavi of the Tamil and he wrote the Kuyil and the Kannan Pattu
He was of the ninth century
explanation: The Subramania Bharati, the Mahakavi of the Tamil, wrote the Kuyil and the Kannan Pattu and the song of the Kodikkarai and he was a contemporary of the Bharathiar and the Ramalingam.

q: The Chera, the Chola and the Pandya were:
options: the three kingdoms of the Sangam age
the Pallava, the Satavahana and the Vakataka
explanation: The three kingdoms of the Sangam age were the Chera of the west, the Chola of the east and the Pandya of the south and the Satiyaputro, the rulers of the Chera, were the contemporaries of the Karikala of the Chola.

q: The Amir Khusrau of the Delhi is:
options: the court poet of the Alauddin Khalji and the father of the Urdu literature
a Sanskrit poet of the Vijayanagara
explanation: The Amir Khusrau, the court poet of the Alauddin Khalji, is called the father of the Urdu literature and he wrote in the Persian, the Arabic, the Turkish and the Hindavi.

q: Which of the following statements about the Faiz Ahmed Faiz is correct?
options: He was the court poet of the Mughals
The Faiz Ahmed Faiz wrote in the Urdu and the Persian and he received the Lenin Peace Prize
explanation: The Faiz Ahmed Faiz wrote the revolutionary Urdu poetry and he received the Lenin Peace Prize in 1963, and the poems like the Mujh Se Pehli Si and the Dast-e-Saba are the landmarks of the Urdu literature.

q: The Mir Taqi Mir was:
options: the successor of the Bahadur Shah
the founder of the Urdu poetry and the author of the Sahr-e-Ilm
explanation: The Mir Taqi Mir, with the Mirza Dabeer, founded the Urdu poetry and his Sahr-e-Ilm is the landmark of the ghazal tradition.

q: The Premchand wrote the Godan and the Nirmala and the Godaan and he was:
explanation: The Premchand, the greatest of the Hindi novelists, wrote the Godan, the Nirmala, the Ghadar and the Raag and he received the Lenin Peace Prize in 1963.

q: Which of the following statements about the R.K. Narayan is correct?
options: He was the master of the Kannada literature
The R.K. Narayan wrote the Guide and the Malgudi Days and the Bachelor of Arts
explanation: The R.K. Narayan of the Malgudi series wrote the Guide, the Malgudi Days and the Bachelor of Arts and his works were adapted into films by the Satyajit Ray and the Shyam Benegal.

q: The Rashid of the Mughal court was:
options: He was a saint of the Punjab
The Rashid was the court poet of the Jahangir and the author of the Gulzar-i-Adlami
He was a poet of the Akbar
He was a writer of the Deccan
explanation: The Rashid, the court poet of the Jahangir, wrote the Gulzar-i-Adlami, the translation of the Mahabharata in the Persian, and the Dara Shikoh and the Faizi were the other court poets.

q: The Vande Mataram is:
options: It was composed by the Nehru
The Vande Mataram is the national song of India and it appeared in the Anandamath of the Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in 1876
explanation: The Vande Mataram, composed by the Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay in the Anandamath of 1876, is the national song of India, and the Jana Gana Mana by the Rabindranath Tagore is the national anthem.

q: The Rabindranath Tagore is:
options: The Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for the Gitanjali
explanation: The Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for the translated Gitanjali and he was the first non-European laureate and the first Asian Nobel laureate.

q: The Sri Aurobindo was:
options: The Sri Aurobindo wrote the Savitri and the Bhagavad Gita and he founded the Ashram at Pondicherry
He was a Bengali poet of the 19th century
explanation: The Sri Aurobindo wrote the Savitri, the epic poem on the life of the Sita, and he founded the Auroville Ashram at Pondicherry with the Mirra Alfassa, the Mother.

q: The Bharatendu Harishchandra is:
options: The Bharatendu Harishchandra is called the father of the modern Hindi literature
He was a poet of the Sanskrit
He was a court poet of the Bahadur Shah
explanation: The Bharatendu Harishchandra is called the father of the modern Hindi literature and the Mahavir Prasad Dwivedi and the Sumitranandan Pant are the other landmarks of the Hindi literature.

q: The Mulk Raj Anand wrote the Untouchable and the Coolie and he was:
options: a founder of the Progressive Writers' Association
explanation: The Mulk Raj Anand, with the Premchand and the Raja Rao, was a founder of the Progressive Writers' Association in 1936 and he wrote the Untouchable and the Coolie.

q: The Girish Karnad was:
options: a filmmaker of the parallel cinema only
a Jnanpith Awardee and a playwright of the Tughlaq and the Kaagaz Te Patte
explanation: The Girish Karnad, a Jnanpith laureate of 1998, was a doyen of the Indian theatre and the recipient of the Padma Shri and the Padma Bhushan.

q: The 'Vyas Samman' is awarded for:
options: A distinguished contribution to the literary work in the Hindi language
A contribution to the Sanskrit literature
A contribution to the English literature
explanation: The Vyas Samman is the prestigious award for a distinguished contribution to the literary work in the Hindi language and it is given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith.

q: The 'Sahitya Akademi Award' is given for:
options: A contribution to the performing arts
A contribution to the scientific research
A distinguished contribution to the literature in one of the 24 languages
A contribution to the English literature only
explanation: The Sahitya Akademi Award, instituted in 1954, is given for a distinguished contribution to the literature in any of the 24 languages recognized by the Constitution.

q: The 'Jnanpith Award' is given for:
options: A contribution to the drama only
A contribution to the poetry only
A distinguished contribution to the literature in any language
explanation: The Jnanpith Award, instituted in 1961, is the highest literary honour of India and it is given for a distinguished contribution to the literature in any language.

q: The Sahridaya awards are:
options: the music awards given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi
the literary awards of the Sahitya Akademi
the film awards given by the Directorate of Film Festivals
the theatre awards given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi
explanation: The Sahridaya awards are the literary awards of the Sahitya Akademi, presented for each of the languages that the Akademi recognises at its Festival of Letters in New Delhi.

q: The Vyas Samman is:
options: given by the Sangeet Natak Akademi
given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith for the Hindi literature
given by the Film Federation of India
explanation: The Vyas Samman is given by the Bharatiya Jnanpith for a distinguished contribution to the Hindi literature.

q: The Diwali festival is:
options: It marks the birth of the Buddha
It marks the birth of the Guru Nanak
Diwali falls on the new moon of the Kartika and it marks the return of the Ramas to Ayodhya
explanation: The Diwali, on the new moon of the Kartika, commemorates the return of the Lord Rama to Ayodhya after the fourteen years of the exile and it is also the day of the Lakshmi Puja.

q: The Holi festival is:
options: Holi marks the arrival of spring and the colours celebrate the destruction of the evil Puthana
It marks the death of the Buddha
explanation: The Holi, the festival of the colours, marks the arrival of spring and it celebrates the destruction of the demon Puthana by the child Krishna.

q: The Eid ul-Fitr and the Eid al-Adha are:
options: They mark the Hindu new year
They mark the birth of the Prophet
The Eid ul-Fitr marks the end of the Ramadan and the Eid al-Adha the end of the Hajj
explanation: The Eid ul-Fitr marks the end of the Ramadan and the Eid al-Adha, the festival of the sacrifice, the end of the Hajj.

q: The Mahavir Jayanti is:
options: The Mahavir Jayanti marks the birth of the Mahavira, the last tirthankara, and the Mahavira was the 24th
It marks the birth of the Buddha
It marks the Nirvana of the Mahavira
It marks the first sermon of the Buddha
explanation: The Mahavir Jayanti marks the birth of the Mahavira, the 24th and the last of the Jain tirthankaras, and it is also the Mahavir Nirvan Kalyanak.

q: The 'Pongal' is a four-day harvest festival of:
explanation: The Pongal, the harvest festival of the Tamil Nadu, celebrates the end of the winter season and the beginning of the harvest and the sun, the cattle and the agriculture are thanked.

q: The 'Bihu' is the festival of:
explanation: The Bihu, the Assamese festival of the spring, the new year and the harvest, marks the arrival of the spring season and the start of the agricultural year.

q: The Onam festival is:
options: It is the harvest festival of the Assam
It is the festival of the Bengal
The Onam is the harvest festival of Kerala with the Pookalam and the Vallam Kali
It is the festival of the Punjab
explanation: The Onam, the harvest festival of the Kerala, is marked by the Pookalam, the flower carpet, the Vallam Kali, the snake boat race, and the display of the Onapottan.

q: The 'Chhath' is a festival of:
options: Bihar and the eastern Uttar Pradesh
explanation: The Chhath, the sun worship festival, is celebrated in the Bihar and the eastern Uttar Pradesh with the devotees standing in the water to offer the arghya to the setting and the rising sun.

q: The Guru Nanak Jayanti is:
options: It is celebrated in the Baisakhi
It is celebrated in the Magha
It marks the death of the Guru
The birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru is celebrated in the Kartika and it is the Gurpurab
explanation: The Guru Nanak Jayanti, the birth anniversary of the first Sikh Guru, is celebrated on the full moon of the Kartika and it is also the Gurpurab.

q: The 'Vaisakhi' is:
options: The harvest festival of the Assam
The harvest festival of the Punjab and the day of the formation of the Khalsa in 1699
explanation: The Vaisakhi, celebrated on 13 or 14 April, is the harvest festival of the Punjab and it marks the founding of the Khalsa by the Guru Gobind Singh in 1699.

q: The 'Gudi Padwa' is the:
options: Marathi new year and the celebration of the hindu Maharashtra
explanation: The Gudi Padwa, the Marathi new year, is celebrated on the first day of the Chaitra and the Uttarakhand and the Gudi flags are hoisted.

q: The 'Puthandu' is the:
options: Tamil new year on the first day of the Tamil month of Chithirai
explanation: The Puthandu, the Tamil new year, falls on the first day of the Tamil month of Chithirai, usually in the middle of April.

q: The Bihu of Assam and the Baisakhi of the Punjab are:
options: the religious festivals of the temples
explanation: The Bihu of the Assam and the Baisakhi of the Punjab are the harvest festivals that mark the new year and the agricultural cycle of the region.

q: The 'Ganesh Chaturthi' marks the:
explanation: The Ganesh Chaturthi, in the Bhadrapada, marks the birth of the Lord Ganesha and it was made a public holiday in 1893 by the British.

q: The Janmashtami festival is:
options: It marks the birth of the Rama
It marks the death of the Krishna
It marks the coronation of the Rama
Janmashtami marks the birth of the Krishna
explanation: The Janmashtami, the birth day of the Krishna, is celebrated in the Bhadrapada and the Dahi Handi and the Janmashtami of the Mathura and the Vrindavan are the famous ones.

q: Raksha Bandhan is:
options: a festival of the brother and the sister
explanation: The Raksha Bandhan, on the full moon of the Shravana, is the festival of the brother and the sister in which the sister ties a rakhi on the wrist of the brother.

q: The Yajnavalkya and the Nirank are:
explanation: The Yajnavalkya Samhita and the Nirukta are the Vedic texts of the ritual and the exegesis and the Vedas, the Brahmanas, the Aranyakas and the Upanishads are the four Vedas.

q: The Ram Navami festival is:
options: It marks the birth of the Krishna
It marks the death of the Rama
It is celebrated in the Kartika
The Ram Navami marks the birth of the Rama and the Chaitra is the month
explanation: The Ram Navami, on the ninth day of the Chaitra, marks the birth of the Rama and it is celebrated with the processions and the kirtans.

q: The Buddha Purnima is:
options: It marks the death of the Guru Nanak
The Buddha Purnima marks the birth, the enlightenment and the death of the Buddha
It marks the birth of the Mahavira
It marks the first sermon of the Buddha
explanation: The Buddha Purnima, on the full moon of the Vaisakha, marks the birth, the enlightenment and the death of the Buddha.

q: The 'Asalha Puja' marks the:
options: The first sermon of the Buddha at the Sarnath
explanation: The Asalha Puja, on the full moon of the Ashadha, commemorates the first sermon of the Buddha at the Sarnath, the Dhamma and the Noble Eightfold Path.

q: The 'Navroz' is the:
options: Persian new year and the spring festival of the Parsis and the Kashmiri Muslims
The new year of the Tamils
explanation: The Navroz, falling on 21 March, is the Persian new year and it is celebrated by the Parsis in India and by the Kashmiri Muslims.

q: The 'Kumbh Mela' at the Prayagraj is held every:
explanation: The Kumbh Mela at the Prayagraj, the Nashik and the Ujjain and the Haridwar is held every twelve years and it is the largest of the human gatherings on the earth.

q: The 'Kumbh Mela' was inscribed as the intangible heritage of the humanity in:
explanation: The Kumbh Mela was inscribed on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity by UNESCO in 2017.

q: The 'Kumbh Mela' at the Nashik is also known as:
explanation: The Kumbh Mela at the Nashik is the Simhastha and it is held every twelve years on the Godavari, while the Prayagraj one is the Maha Kumbh.

q: The 'World Heritage List' of the UNESCO started in:
explanation: The World Heritage List was inscribed for the first time in 1978 with the Convention of 1972 and India has the sites of the Ajanta, the Ellora, the Sanchi and the Agra from the first batch.

q: The Indian elements on the UNESCO intangible heritage list include:
options: The Indian elements include the Yoga, the Kumbh Mela, the Kutiyattam, the Ramlila, the Chhau, the Kalbelia and the Kumbh
Only the Yoga is from India
Only the Kumbh Mela is from India
explanation: The Indian elements on the Representative List include the Yoga, the Kumbh Mela, the Kutiyattam, the Ramlila, the Chhau, the Kalbelia, the Vedic chanting and the Budhya Stree Mela.

q: The 'UNESCO Creative Cities' of India:
options: Jaipur for the crafts and the folk art and Varanasi for the crafts
explanation: Jaipur was inscribed as a UNESCO Creative City for the Crafts and the Folk Art in 2014 and Varanasi for the Creative Crafts in 2015.

q: The Kaziranga, the Manas and the Periyar are:
explanation: The Project Elephant reserves include the Kaziranga, the Manas, the Periyar, the Bhadra, the Nagarhole, the Similipal and the Parambikulam.

q: The Madras Naturalists Society was:
options: founded in 1877 and the Madras Museum in 1851
explanation: The Madras Naturalists' Society, founded in 1877, had the Madras Museum in 1851 as its antecedent and the museum is one of the oldest of its kind in the country.

q: The Archaeological Survey of India was founded in 1861 and it is:
explanation: The Archaeological Survey of India, founded in 1861 under the Alexander Cunningham, functions under the Ministry of Culture and it protects more than 3,500 monuments.

q: The 'National Museum' of India was founded in:
explanation: The National Museum was founded in 1949 in the erstwhile Prince of Wales' Museum at Delhi and it has one of the largest collections of the Indian art.

q: The 'Calico Museum' of the Textiles is at:
explanation: The Calico Museum of the Textiles, with one of the world's largest collections of the textiles, is at Ahmedabad and it is a national museum of the textiles.

q: The 'Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya' was earlier known as:
explanation: The Prince of Wales Museum in Mumbai was renamed the Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya and it houses one of the finest collections of the decorative arts.

q: The 'Salarjung Museum' is at:
explanation: The Salarjung Museum at Hyderabad, with a collection of over 40,000 objects, is one of the largest museums in the world.

q: The Great Stupa at Sanchi is:
options: The Sanchi was built by the Ashoka and the gateways were added later
The Sanchi was built by the Ashoka and the gateways are of the Gupta period
It was built by the Kanishka
It was built by the Satavahanas
explanation: The Great Stupa at Sanchi was commissioned by the Ashoka and the elaborately carved gateways were added in the subsequent centuries, mainly in the Satavahana and the Gupta periods.

q: The Bateshwar temples in the Madhya Pradesh are:
options: a group of the 51 Shaiva temples of the Paramara dynasty
explanation: The Bateshwar group of the 51 Shaiva temples in the Madhya Pradesh was built by the Paramara king Bhoja and it is one of the finest examples of the Central Indian temple architecture.

q: The Chausath Yogini temple of the 9th century is:
options: in the Madhya Pradesh and is a circular shrine with 64 cells
explanation: The Chausath Yogini temple at the Morena in the Madhya Pradesh is a circular shrine of the 9th century with 64 cells and it is a unique structure.

q: The 'Rani ki Vav' at Patan was built in the:
options: 11th century and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site
explanation: The Rani ki Vav, the stepwell of the Solanki king Bhima I, was built in the 11th century at Patan in the Gujarat and it was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2014.

q: The Konark temple of the Odisha is:
options: a chariot of the Surya and it was built by the Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga
explanation: The Konark temple, the chariot of the sun god, was built by the Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty in the 13th century and it is a World Heritage site.

q: The Khangchendzonga National Park is:
options: The Khangchendzonga National Park in the Sikkim was inscribed in 2016 and it protects the snow leopard
explanation: The Khangchendzonga National Park, inscribed as a mixed cultural and natural World Heritage site in 2016, protects the snow leopard, the red panda and the Himalayan tiger.

q: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus of the Mumbai was:
explanation: The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, the Victorian Gothic and Art Deco ensemble of the Mumbai, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2004.

q: The Agra Fort was:
options: inscribed in 1983 and the Red Fort in 1993
explanation: The Agra Fort was inscribed in 1983 in the first batch and the Red Fort Complex of Delhi in 1993.

q: The Martand temple is:
options: the 8th century temple of the sun god in the Kashmir
explanation: The Martand or the Martand temple of the sun, of the 8th century, is in the Kashmir and it is one of the finest of the Hindu temples of the early period.

q: The Ellora caves are:
options: They are only the Buddhist caves
They were built in the 18th century
The Ellora caves, of the 1st to the 10th century, show the Buddhist, the Hindu and the Jain rock-cut architecture
explanation: The Ellora caves, cut between the 6th and the 10th centuries, contain the Buddhist, the Hindu and the Jain monuments and they were inscribed in 1983.

q: The Hampi group of monuments, the ruins of the Vijayanagara was:
explanation: The Group of Monuments at Hampi, the ruins of the Vijayanagara capital, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1986.

q: The 'Rock-Hewn Churches' of the Goa were inscribed in:
explanation: The Churches and the Convents of the Goa, with the Rock-Hewn Churches, were inscribed as a World Heritage site in 1986.

q: Great Himalayan National Park was:
options: inscribed in 2014 for the outstanding natural beauty and the diverse habitats
explanation: The Great Himalayan National Park in the Himachal Pradesh was inscribed in 2014 and it is a biosphere reserve as well.

q: They were inscribed in 1984 and they are:
explanation: The Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram, the rock-cut caves and the Shore Temple of the Pallava period, was inscribed in 1984.

q: The Rani ki Vav at Patan is:
options: a stepwell and it was inscribed in 2014
explanation: The Rani ki Vav, the stepwell of the 11th century at Patan, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2014.

q: The Dhol Vikram is:
options: a Buddhist stupa of the Bihar
a temple of the Tamil Nadu
a Neolithic site in the Gujarat and it was inscribed in 2021
explanation: The Dhol Vikram, a Neolithic settlement of the 3rd millennium BCE in the Gujarat, was inscribed as a World Heritage site in 2021.

q: Consider the following statements. Which of them is correct with regard to the inscribed 2023?
options: inscribed in 2023 for the ashram and the university campus of the Tagore
explanation: The Santiniketan, the ashram and the university campus of the Rabindranath Tagore, was inscribed as a World Heritage cultural site in 2023.

q: The Jhansi Fort is:
options: a UNESCO World Heritage site as a part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan
explanation: The Jhansi Fort, built by the Orchha ruler Bir Singh Deo, was inscribed in 2013 as a part of the Hill Forts of Rajasthan group.
